newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bertelsmann director sees pay TV accord.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann director sees pay TV accord.

text.p: German pay TV channel Premiere, owned by Bertelsmann and France's Canal Plus, could reach an accord with press magnate Leo Kirch over a joint programme offering by the summer, a Bertelsmann board director told daily newspaper La Tribune on Wednesday.
"I talk with Leo Kirch more than people think and I am certain we can reach an accord, at the latest by the summer. DF1 cannot develop without Premiere," Michael Dornemann said.
Currently, press magnate Leo Kirch partners Bertelsmann and France's Canal Plus's channel Premiere, and has his own programme offering called DF1.
Dornemann said there was only room for one pay television offering in Germany, and it should be a common one.
"There is no room in Germany for two offerings, especially as prices of film rights and of sports coverage have reached new heights," he said.
"Pay television is a promising market, but at best it will represent 20 to 25 percent of the total in Germany, or 12.55 billion marks currently," Dornemann said.
Bertelsmann and Canal Plus each have 37.5 percent of Premiere, while Leo Kirch has 25 percent.
